questions.question: Statement I: In coagulation of negative sol, flocculating power is Al³⁺ > Ba²⁺ > Na⁺. Statement II: In coagulation of positive sol, flocculating power is NaCl > Na₂SO₄ > Na₃PO₄.

options.A: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
options.B: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
options.C: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
options.D: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.explanation: By Hardy-Schulze rule, higher valence of flocculating ion = greater power. Statement I correct (Al³⁺ > Ba²⁺ > Na⁺). Statement II incorrect: for positive sol, order should be PO₄³⁻ > SO₄²⁻ > Cl⁻, so Na₃PO₄ > Na₂SO₄ > NaCl.

questions.question: Which statement regarding polymers is NOT correct?

options.B: Thermoplastic polymers are capable of repeatedly softening and hardening on heating and cooling.
options.D: Elastomers have polymer chains held together by weak intermolecular forces.

questions.explanation: Thermosetting polymers are NOT reusable — they undergo permanent cross-linking on heating and cannot be reshaped.

questions.question: The incorrect statement regarding chirality is:

options.A: SN2 reaction of haloalkane having chirality at reactive site shows inversion of configuration.
options.B: Enantiomers are superimposable mirror images of each other.
options.C: A racemic mixture shows zero optical rotation.
options.D: SN1 reaction yields 1:1 mixture of both enantiomers.

questions.explanation: Enantiomers are NON-superimposable mirror images, not superimposable ones.

questions.question: RMgX + CO₂ → Y → H₃O⁺ → RCOOH. What is Y?
questions.explanation: Grignard reagent reacts with CO₂: RMgX + CO₂ → RCOOMgX (Y). On hydrolysis with H₃O⁺, gives RCOOH.

questions.question: In one molal solution containing 0.5 mole of solute, there is:
questions.explanation: Molality m = (moles of solute/weight of solvent in g) × 1000. 1 = (0.5/W) × 1000. W = 500 g of solvent.

questions.question: Match hydrides with their nature: (a) MgH₂, (b) GeH₄, (c) B₂H₆, (d) HF with (i) Electron precise, (ii) Electron deficient, (iii) Electron rich, (iv) Ionic
questions.explanation: MgH₂ → ionic. GeH₄ → electron precise (8e, no lone pair). B₂H₆ → electron deficient (less than 8e). HF → electron rich (lone pairs present).

questions.question: Statement I: BP of aldehydes/ketones > hydrocarbons of comparable mass (due to dipole-dipole). Statement II: BP of aldehydes/ketones < alcohols of similar mass (due to absence of H-bonding).

options.A: Both Statements I and II are incorrect.
options.B: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
options.C: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
options.D: Both Statements I and II are correct.

questions.explanation: Both are correct. BP order: R-OH > Aldehyde/Ketone > Alkane. Aldehyde/ketone > alkane (dipole-dipole); alcohol > aldehyde/ketone (H-bonding).

questions.question: Match products formed from carbonyl compound reactions: (a) Cyanohydrin, (b) Acetal, (c) Schiff's base, (d) Oxime with reagents (i) NH₂OH, (ii) RNH₂, (iii) alcohol, (iv) HCN
questions.explanation: Cyanohydrin: C=O + HCN. Acetal: C=O + 2ROH(alcohol). Schiff's base: C=O + RNH₂. Oxime: C=O + NH₂OH.

questions.question: Which is NOT the correct mathematical equation for Dalton's Law of partial pressure (p = total pressure)?
questions.explanation: Option C is Raoult's law (for solutions), not Dalton's law. In Dalton's law: pi = χi × P (total pressure of gaseous mixture), not pi°(pure gas pressure).

questions.question: Match drug classes with drug molecules: (a) Antacids, (b) Antihistamines, (c) Analgesics, (d) Antimicrobials with (i) Salvarsan, (ii) Morphine, (iii) Cimetidine, (iv) Seldane
questions.explanation: Antacid → Cimetidine. Antihistamine → Seldane. Analgesic → Morphine. Antimicrobial → Salvarsan.

questions.question: Statement I: BP of group 16 hydrides increases as H₂O < H₂S < H₂Se < H₂Te. Statement II: BP of these hydrides increases with molar mass.

options.A: Both Statements I and II are incorrect.
options.B: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
options.C: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
options.D: Both Statements I and II are correct.

questions.explanation: Both incorrect. Correct BP order: H₂S < H₂Se < H₂Te < H₂O (H₂O is highest due to strong H-bonding, anomalous). Statement II incorrect because H₂O has highest BP despite lowest molar mass.

questions.question: IUPAC name of complex [Ag(H₂O)₂][Ag(CN)₂] is:
questions.explanation: Coordination number = 2. Ag has oxidation state +1. Cation: [Ag(H₂O)₂]⁺ = diaquasilver(I). Anion: [Ag(CN)₂]⁻ = dicyanidoargentate(I).

questions.question: Which method is suitable to synthesize chlorobenzene?
questions.explanation: Chlorobenzene is synthesized by electrophilic aromatic substitution: Benzene + Cl₂ with anhydrous FeCl₃ (Lewis acid catalyst) → Chlorobenzene + HCl.

questions.question: Assertion (A): ICl is more reactive than I₂. Reason (R): I-Cl bond is weaker than I-I bond.

options.A: Both A and R are correct but R is not correct explanation of A.
options.B: A is correct but R is not correct.
options.C: A is not correct but R is correct.
options.D: Both A and R are correct and R is correct explanation of A.

questions.explanation: ICl is more reactive because I-Cl bond (interhalogen) is weaker than I-I bond (as X-X' < X-X except F). Both A and R are correct and R explains A.

questions.question: IUPAC name of element with atomic number 119 is:
questions.explanation: 119 → 1=un, 1=un, 9=enn → Ununennium (Uue).

questions.question: E°(Cu²⁺/Cu)=0.34V, E°(Zn²⁺/Zn)=-0.76V, E°(Fe²⁺/Fe)=-0.44V, E°(Ag⁺/Ag)=0.80V. Which reaction cannot occur?
questions.explanation: Reactivity: Zn > Fe > Cu > Ag. Less reactive metals cannot displace more reactive metals from solutions. Ag cannot displace Cu (Cu is less reactive than Ag is false — actually Cu > Ag in reactivity). E°cell = 0.34 - 0.80 = -0.46V < 0. Reaction not spontaneous.

questions.question: Which compound is NOT an aromatic compound?
questions.explanation: Per official answer key, option (3) which is the cyclohexa-1,3-diene (non-aromatic, sp³ carbon present). Aromatic: 4n+2 π electrons, planar, cyclic, all sp² carbons.

questions.question: Choose the correct statement about diamond and graphite:

options.A: Diamond is covalent and graphite is ionic.
options.B: Diamond is sp³ hybridised and graphite is sp² hybridised.
options.C: Both diamond and graphite are used as dry lubricants.
options.D: Diamond and graphite have two dimensional network.

questions.explanation: Diamond: each C bonded to 4 others → sp³. Graphite: each C bonded to 3 others → sp².

questions.question: Statement I: Primary aliphatic amines react with HNO₂ to give unstable diazonium salts. Statement II: Primary aromatic amines react with HNO₂ to form diazonium salts stable even above 300 K.

options.A: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
options.B: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
options.C: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
options.D: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.explanation: Statement I correct: aliphatic diazonium salts (R-N₂⁺) are unstable. Statement II incorrect: aryl diazonium salts are stable only at low temperature (0-5°C), NOT above 300K.

questions.question: Assertion (A): In a point defect, ionic solid is electrically neutral even if few cations are missing from unit cells. Reason (R): In Frenkel defect, cation dislocates from lattice to interstitial site, maintaining overall electrical neutrality.

options.A: Both A and R are correct but R is not correct explanation of A.
options.B: A is correct but R is not correct.
options.C: A is not correct but R is correct.
options.D: Both A and R are correct and R is correct explanation of A.

questions.explanation: A is correct (metal deficiency defect maintains neutrality). R is correct (Frenkel defect description). But R is not correct explanation of A — metal deficiency defect involves Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺ substitution, not Frenkel defect.

questions.question: Kjeldahl's method for nitrogen estimation can be used for which compound?
questions.explanation: Kjeldahl's method is NOT applicable to compounds with nitro, azo groups or nitrogen in ring (pyridine). It works for aniline (primary aryl amine).

questions.question: Which P-V curve represents maximum work done?
questions.explanation: Work done = area under P-V curve. Maximum area under curve = maximum work done. Graph 1 has maximum area.

questions.question: Which statement about diborane is NOT correct?

options.A: Four terminal B-H bonds are two centre two electron bonds.
options.B: Four terminal hydrogen atoms and two boron atoms lie in one plane.
options.C: Both boron atoms are sp² hybridised.

questions.explanation: In diborane (B₂H₆), boron atoms are sp³ hybridised (not sp²), making it non-planar.

questions.question: pH of solution containing 50 mL each of 0.10 M sodium acetate and 0.01 M acetic acid is: [pKa of CH₃COOH = 4.57]
Which is INCORRECT statement about molecular orbital theory?

options.A: C₂ molecule has four electrons in two degenerate π molecular orbitals.
options.D: Bond orders of O₂⁺, O₂, O₂⁻ and O₂²⁻ are 2.5, 2, 1.5 and 1 respectively.

questions.explanation: O₂⁻ has 17 electrons (one extra from O₂'s 16). Configuration has 1 unpaired electron in π* orbital → paramagnetic, NOT diamagnetic.

questions.question: Which molecule will have maximum lone pair–lone pair electron repulsions?
questions.explanation: XeF₂: sp³d hybridised, linear shape with 3 lone pairs on equatorial positions. 3 lone pairs in equatorial plane give maximum lp-lp repulsions.

questions.question: Mass of 95% pure CaCO₃ required to neutralise 50 mL of 0.5 M HCl is: [Calculate to 2 decimal places]
Identify the INCORRECT statement:

options.A: The oxidation number of K in KO₂ is +4.
options.B: Ionisation enthalpy of alkali metals decreases from top to bottom in the group.
options.C: Lithium is the strongest reducing agent among alkali metals.
options.D: Alkali metals react with water to form their hydroxides.

questions.explanation: In KO₂, K is +1 and O₂ is superoxide ion (O₂⁻). Oxidation number of K = +1, not +4.

questions.question: Gadolinium has low value of third ionisation enthalpy because of:
questions.explanation: Gd: [Xe]6s²4f⁷5d¹. Gd²⁺: [Xe]4f⁷5d¹. Removing 5d electron gives stable half-filled 4f⁷ configuration with high exchange energy. Hence low 3rd ionisation enthalpy.

questions.question: Graph of kinetics at constant T: y-axis and x-axis for zero and first order reactions respectively are:

options.A: Zero order (y=concentration, x=time); first order (y=rate constant, x=concentration)
options.B: Zero order (y=rate, x=concentration); first order (y=t½, x=concentration)
options.C: Zero order (y=rate, x=concentration); first order (y=rate, x=t½)
options.D: Zero order (y=concentration, x=time); first order (y=t½, x=concentration)

questions.explanation: Zero order: rate is constant (doesn't depend on concentration) → rate vs concentration = horizontal line. First order: t½ = 0.693/k (independent of concentration) → t½ vs concentration = horizontal line.

questions.question: Kjeldahl's method for nitrogen estimation can be used for compounds containing nitrogen in which form? (Identify incorrect compound)
questions.explanation: Kjeldahl's method NOT applicable for nitro, azo, or ring nitrogen (pyridine). Only works for amine nitrogen. Aniline (ArNH₂) can be estimated. Ans per official key: (2) i.e. aniline.

questions.question: Identify the INCORRECT statement from the following about d-orbitals:

options.A: All five 4d orbitals have shapes similar to respective 3d orbitals.
options.B: In an atom, all five 3d orbitals are equal in energy in free state.
options.C: Shapes of dxy, dyz and dzx are similar to each other; and dx²-y² and dz² are similar to each other.
options.D: All five 5d orbitals are different in size when compared to respective 4d orbitals.

questions.explanation: dxy, dyz, dzx are similar in shape (clover leaf between axes). But dx²-y² is also clover leaf (along axes) while dz² has a different shape (dumbbell with torus). So option 3 is incorrect.

questions.question: Half cell reactions: MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O, E° = -1.510V; ½O₂ + 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂O, E° = +1.223V. Will MnO₄⁻ liberate O₂ from water in acid?
questions.explanation: Target: 2MnO₄⁻ + 6H⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + 5/2O₂ + 3H₂O. E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode = 1.510 - 1.223 = +0.287V > 0. Reaction is spontaneous. Yes, O₂ is liberated.

questions.question: Match: (a) Li, (b) Na, (c) KOH, (d) Cs with (i) Absorbent for CO₂, (ii) Electrochemical cells, (iii) Coolant in fast breeder reactors, (iv) Photoelectric cell
questions.explanation: Li → electrochemical cells. Na → coolant in fast breeder reactors. KOH → absorbent for CO₂. Cs → photoelectric cell (low ionisation energy).

questions.question: Statement I: Acidic strength of monosubstituted nitrophenol is higher than phenol due to electron withdrawing nitro group. Statement II: o-, m- and p-nitrophenol have same acidic strength as they have one nitro group.

options.A: Both Statement I and II are incorrect.
options.B: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
options.C: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
options.D: Both Statement I and II are correct.

questions.explanation: Statement I correct: -NO₂ is EWG, increases acidity. Statement II incorrect: acidic strength order is p-NO₂ > o-NO₂ > m-NO₂ phenol (different positions have different effects).

questions.question: Pollution due to oxides of sulphur is enhanced by presence of: (a) particulate matter, (b) ozone, (c) hydrocarbons, (d) hydrogen peroxide
questions.explanation: Particulate matter catalyses SO₂ → SO₃. Ozone: SO₂ + O₃ → SO₃ + O₂. H₂O₂: SO₂ + H₂O₂ → H₂SO₄. Hydrocarbons do not enhance SO₂ oxidation directly.

questions.question: Correct IUPAC name of compound: CH₃CH(Cl)CH(CH₃)CH(OH)CH₂Br is:
questions.explanation: Numbering from Br end: 1-bromo, 3-ol, 4-methyl, 5-chloro on hexane chain. IUPAC: 1-bromo-5-chloro-4-methylhexan-3-ol.

questions.question: 3O₂(g) ⇌ 2O₃(g); Kc = 3.0 × 10⁻⁵⁹ at 298K. [O₂] at equilibrium = 0.040 M. Concentration of O₃ in M is:
Match ores with composition: (a) Haematite, (b) Magnetite, (c) Calamine, (d) Kaolinite with (i) Fe₃O₄, (ii) ZnCO₃, (iii) Fe₂O₃, (iv) Al₂(OH)₄Si₂O₅
questions.explanation: Haematite = Fe₂O₃. Magnetite = Fe₃O₄. Calamine = ZnCO₃. Kaolinite = Al₂(OH)₄Si₂O₅.

questions.question: Statement I: In Lucas test, 1°, 2°, 3° alcohols are distinguished by reactivity with conc. HCl + ZnCl₂. Statement II: Primary alcohols are most reactive and immediately produce turbidity at room temperature.

options.A: Both Statements I and II are incorrect.
options.B: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
options.C: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
options.D: Both Statements I and II are correct.

questions.explanation: Statement I correct. Statement II incorrect: 3° alcohols give immediate turbidity; 2° in ~5 min; 1° take ~30 min. So primary is LEAST reactive, not most.

questions.question: In neutral/faintly alkaline medium, KMnO₄ oxidises iodide to iodate. Change in oxidation state of manganese is:
questions.explanation: In neutral/faintly alkaline medium: KMnO₄ + I⁻ → MnO₂ + IO₃⁻. Mn changes from +7 (KMnO₄) to +4 (MnO₂).

questions.question: First order reaction A → Products. Initial [A] = 0.1M, becomes 0.001M after 5 min. Rate constant in min⁻¹ is:
Compound X on reaction with O₃ then Zn/H₂O gives formaldehyde and 2-methylpropanal. Compound X is:
questions.explanation: Ozonolysis of 3-methylbut-1-ene (CH₃CH(CH₃)CH=CH₂): gives HCHO (formaldehyde) from =CH₂ end and (CH₃)₂CHCHO (2-methylpropanal) from other end.

questions.question: A 10.0 L flask contains 64 g O₂ at 27°C. (Assume O₂ is ideal). Pressure inside flask in bar is: [R = 0.0831 L bar K⁻¹ mol⁻¹]
Order of energy absorbed for colour of complexes: (A) [Ni(H₂O)₂(en)₂]²⁺, (B) [Ni(H₂O)₄(en)]²⁺, (C) [Ni(en)₃]²⁺ is:
questions.explanation: en is strong field ligand (SFL). More en → larger crystal field splitting Δ0 → more energy absorbed. C(3 en) > A(2 en) > B(1 en).

questions.question: Which product is NOT formed when acetone reacts with 2-pentanone in presence of dilute NaOH followed by heating?

options.B: A cross-aldol product with CH₃ and longer chain

questions.explanation: In cross-aldol condensation of acetone and 2-pentanone, certain cross products form but 4-methylpent-3-en-2-one (from self-aldol of acetone) will NOT form under these mixed conditions as per answer key.

questions.question: EMF of cell: Ni(s) + 2Ag⁺(0.001M) → Ni²⁺(0.001M) + 2Ag(s). E°cell = 10.5V (given artificially high for calculation), 2.303RT/F = 0.059 at 298K. EMF is:
questions.explanation: Ecell = E°cell - (0.059/n)log([Ni²⁺]/[Ag⁺]²) = 10.5 - (0.059/2)log(10⁻³/(10⁻³)²) = 10.5 - 0.0295×3 = 10.4115V. Calculated answer not in options → Bonus.

questions.question: Radius of second Bohr orbit of He⁺ = 105.8 pm. Radius of third Bohr orbit of Li²⁺ is:
Copper crystallises in fcc unit cell, edge = 3.608 × 10⁻⁸ cm, density = 8.92 g/cm³. Atomic mass of copper is:
Product formed from: PhCH₂CN → (i) LiAlH₄, H₂O → (ii) NaNO₂, HCl → (iii) H₂O
questions.explanation: PhCH₂CN → LiAlH₄ → PhCH₂CH₂NH₂ → NaNO₂/HCl(0-5°C) → PhCH₂CH₂N₂⁺Cl⁻ → H₂O → PhCH₂CH₂OH. Final product is benzyl carbinol (PhCH₂OH after rearrangement shown in paper).
